 Judgment
Challenging judgment and award dated 14.08.2015 passed by Motor Accident Claims Tribunal No.VI, Vijaypur (for short 'Tribunal') in MVC No.1650/2013, this appeal is filed.

sentences.text:
2. Shri.Bapugouda Siddappa, learned counsel for appellants submitted that appeal was by claimants,
seeking enhancement of compensation and also NC: 2023:KHC-K:7459 challenging dismissal of claim petition against insurer.

It was submitted that on 23.06.2013, Kashinath was riding motorcycle bearing registration no.MH-12/EA-7776 on Kuvarbav-Hathkhamba-Ratnagiri Highway,
Sayabanna @ Sahebrao S/O Bagawant ... vs Suresh S/O Vishnu Padhye And Anr on 19 September, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/164388730/
2 when Maruti Swift Desire Car bearing registration no.MH-08/Z-5333 driven by its driver in rash and negligent manner dashed against it and caused accident.
In said accident, Kashinath sustained grievous injuries and was admitted to hospital, but died during treatment.
Claiming compensation on account of his untimely death, his parents and siblings filed claim petition under Section 166 of Motor Vehicles Act (for short 'M.V. Act') against owner and insurer of car.
3. On service of notice, owner and insurer appeared and filed objections denying negligence on part of driver of car.
Insurer also alleged violation of policy conditions by insured.

Based on pleadings,
Tribunal framed issues and recorded evidence, wherein claimant no.1 was examined as PW.1 and eyewitness as PW.2.
Exs.P1 to P13 were marked.

On behalf of respondents, NC: 2023:KHC-K:7459 official of insurer was examined as RW.1 and got marked insurance policy as Ex.R1.
4.

On consideration, tribunal held that accident had occurred due to rash and negligent driving of car by its driver leading to death of Kashinath and claimants were entitled for compensation of Rs.4,08,000/-.
However, held owner liable to pay compensation on ground that claimants had failed to establish that driver of car had valid and effective driving licence to drive at time of accident.
Claim petition against insurer was dismissed.
It was submitted that merely on basis of charge sheet, there cannot be presumption that driver was driving it in drunken state.
It was also submitted that since owner of vehicle had failed to produce driving licence, award was passed against owner and same was not justified.

5. Insofar as enhancement, it was submitted that though claimants had stated that deceased was 23 years of age, working as driver and earning Rs.8,000/- per month, tribunal has erroneously taken only Rs.4,500/- and NC: 2023:KHC-K:7459 without adding future prospects has awarded inadequate compensation.
Tribunal also erred in applying incorrect multiplier.
It was also submitted that compensation under other heads is also inadequate and sought enhancement.
6. On other hand, Sri Manvendra Reddy, learned counsel for respondent no.2-insurer sought to support award.
It was submitted that driver of vehicle was charge sheeted by police for offences under Sections 3, 181, 184 and 185 of M.V. Act, apart from offences under Indian Penal Code.
This would indicate that driver was prosecuted for causing accident without holding driving licence and in drunken state.
It was submitted that since owner appeared before tribunal, but failed to produce driving licence, tribunal has rightly passed award against owner.
It was further submitted that even before this Court claimants had taken time to produce driving licence, but failed to produce same and therefore, adverse inference ought to be drawn.
Heard learned counsel, perused impugned judgment and award.

8. From above submission and since only claimants are in appeal, challenging finding of tribunal on liability and seeking enhancement, following points would arise for consideration:
"1.
Whether dismissal of claim petition against insurer was justified?

3 2. Whether claimants are entitled for enhancement of compensation?"

Point no.1:
9.

In order to establish actionable negligence against insurer, claimants relied upon FIR,
Statements, Spot Panchanama, Motor Vehicle Inspector's Report and their translations marked as Exs.P1 to P13.
Said deposition was sought to be corroborated by examining eyewitness as PW.2.

Though there was no specific contest regarding manner of occurrence of accident and negligence,
contest of insurer was mainly on two aspects:
NC: 2023:KHC-K:7459 first one was that driver was not having valid and effective driving licence and second was that driver was in drunken state.

To dislodge same,
respondent no.1-owner/insured though entered appearance, did not make any effort before tribunal.
Even claimants who had taken time to produce driving licence before this Court have failed to produce same despite lapse of sufficient time.
Under circumstances, in absence of any specific material, there would be no scope for interference against finding recorded by tribunal.
Moreover, even owner, against whom award has been passed has not preferred appeal.
Hence, point no.1 is answered in negative.

Point no.2:
10.
Insofar as income, though claimants had stated that deceased was earning Rs.8,000/- per month from driving, driving licence was not produced and there is no specific evidence to substantiate income.
Therefore, tribunal was justified in assessing it notionally.
But, notional income for year 2013 is Rs.7,000/- per month.
Therefore, same has to be considered as income of deceased.
Deceased was self-employed, bachelor aged 23 years.

In view of ratio in case of National Insurance Company Limited v. Pranay Sethi and others1, tribunal was not justified in applying multiplier corresponding to younger parent, age of deceased has to be considered.

entities.text: National Insurance Company Limited v. Pranay Sethi and others1
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Claimants would be entitled for addition of '40%' towards future prospects, deduction towards personal expenses has to be at '50%' and multiplier applicable would be '18'.

Thus, total loss of dependency would be:
(Rs.7,000 + 40% - 50%) x 12 x 18 = Rs.10,58,400/-
11.

In addition, as per decision of Hon'ble Supreme Court in Magma General Insurance Company Limited vs. Nanu Ram Alias Chuhru Ram and others2, claimants no.1 and 2 would be entitled for Rs.40,000/- each towards 'loss of parental consortium'.

entities.text: Magma General Insurance Company Limited vs. Nanu Ram Alias Chuhru Ram and others2
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: They would also be entitled for Rs.15,000/- towards 'funeral expenses' and Rs.15,000/- towards 'loss of estate'.

13. Since three years have lapsed after rendering decision in Pranay Sethi's case (supra), claimants would be entitled for addition of 10% on compensation under conventional heads i.e., Rs.11,000/-.

4 14.

Thus, claimants would be entitled for total compensation of Rs.11,79,400/- with interest at 6%
p.a.
Point no.2 is answered partly in affirmative as above.

Consequently, following:
ORDER i. Appeal is allowed in part.
ii. Claimants are entitled for total compensation of Rs.11,79,400/- with interest at 6%
p.a. from date of claim petition till deposit, as against Rs.4,08,000/- awarded by Tribunal.
iii. Dismissal of claim petition against respondent no.2-insurer is confirmed.

- 10 - NC: 2023:KHC-K:7459 iv. Enhanced compensation shall be payable by respondent no.1-owner, who shall deposit same with interest before tribunal within eight weeks from date of receipt of certified copy of this order.
v. On deposit, directions issued by tribunal regarding apportionment, deposit and release shall apply to enhanced compensation also.
